blocks.text: The chapter traces Absalom’s rebellion from preparation to open takeover. He first builds popular support by presenting himself as attentive to people seeking justice. He then arranges for his kingship to be proclaimed at Hebron, while the conspiracy continues to gain followers. The resulting threat drives David and his household from Jerusalem, turning a struggle for influence into a direct contest for the kingdom.

sections.title: The Wider Movement of Second Samuel

blocks.text: Second Samuel begins with David’s accession and the consolidation of his kingdom, then recounts the arrival of the ark and the promise concerning his dynasty. The book subsequently turns toward royal abuse, violence within David’s household, rebellion, and grief before concluding with a four-part appendix. Absalom’s revolt belongs to this later movement of household conflict and rebellion.
